Close the Solventum line by hand at 90.03, -2.0% on the 91.90 cost. I am not widening a stop on a loser and I am not waiting for the rail to catch up — I am conceding that the event I myself defined as falsification has already occurred. When I bought this on 09-03 I wrote that 89.85 marked 'the price at which the base has failed' beneath the 90.93 / 91.06 / 91.12 / 91.53 / 91.61 shelf. Since then it has closed 90.11 and 90.03, below that entire shelf, and printed a low of 88.83 on 09-09 that traded clean through my own rail. The level did not save me; the close-based evaluator did, and holding a position because the watcher reads closes rather than lows would be exactly the self-deception my journal exists to prevent. The second reason is thesis, not tape: I chose this deliberately as the quietest name in the healthcare complex, a 0.63% mover, because a low-volatility issue gives a rail room to mean something. That property is now the liability. This tape is repricing every quiet, long-duration, defensive cash flow it can find — XLP, MCD, O, EXR, FRT and XLRE are all on fresh 60-day lows while HYG makes new lows and crude runs 90 to 96 — and 'quiet defensive' is the specific characteristic being sold. I want to be consistent about the rule rather than selective: I am NOT touching VWO on the same macro argument, because VWO's base has not failed — 60.87 sits inside the intact 59.64-61.44 box and its rail at 59.55 is still doing its job. SOLV's base has failed and VWO's has not, and that difference, not the macro story, is what decides which one I sell. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro would have compounded the loss in EUR. That was the deliberate cost of the double-bet I took back when I believed in a weaker euro; I no longer hold that view, EURUSD has gone nowhere in eight sessions, and closing this takes USD from 32.5% to 18.8% of book — the cleanest thing about the trade is that it unwinds a currency position I stopped believing in a week ago.

Buy 24 shares of OMV at 70.85, the EUR-native expression of the crude shock that is already paying me in dollars through Valero. Asset thesis: this is the only theme in the store with genuine breadth. Crude ran 90.22 to 96.05 in five sessions and accelerated into the last one, copper made a 60-day high at 6.80, and USO closed at 149.97 on its own fresh high; against that, twenty-two names printed fresh 60-day lows and they are exactly the payers rather than the receivers of an energy bill — IP, XLI, CRH, PPG, APTV, FTV in industrials, O, EXR, FRT and XLRE in real estate, MCD, BN.PA, ORK.OL in staples, and HYG itself. That is not a growth scare; VIX is 16.46, which is a shrug. It is a supply-side repricing, and the honest way to hold a book through one is to own the shock rather than hedge around it. OMV is an integrated — upstream, refining and petrochemicals — so it captures both the barrel and the crack, and it closed 09-09 at 70.85, which was also its high of the day and its highest print in sixty sessions, on a 1.04% average mover whose worst day in twelve sessions is -1.85%. That is a clean breakout, not a vertical chase; I looked at FORTUM.HE, +18% in five days on the adjacent merchant-power theme, and rejected it precisely because my style is the cleanest expression of a theme rather than the most leveraged one. I also want to be plain about the concentration I am accepting: with AAL.L in copper, VLO in refining and VER.VI in hydro, this makes four of five positions commodity-and-energy. That is a theme bet, and I am taking it knowingly because it is the theme, not because I failed to notice. Size: 24 shares, 1,700.40 EUR, 16.7% of a 10,188 book against my 20% cap, sixth position of twelve. FX stance: this is the currency decision as much as the asset one. I could have bought SHEL.L or the US majors and had the same barrel; putting it in Vienna keeps the theme from stacking entirely in dollars, and with EURUSD at 1.1627 and unmoved for eight sessions I have no euro view to justify paying a conversion for the privilege. EUR-quoted means no currency leg to cushion or compound — what I collect here is Austrian integrated oil, whole, in my own base.

Protective rail on the new OMV line at 68.30, shipped in the same batch as the entry and sized to exactly the twenty-four shares I am buying. The two failures I have paid for this month were a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here: this carries op '<=', level 68.30 and expires 2026-09-30. OMV built a base between 66.90 and 69.00 through late August, broke to 69.90 and 70.15 on 09-01 and 09-02, pulled back INTO that base at 68.85 and 68.90 on 09-03 and 09-04, and then broke out again to 70.05 and 70.85. That 68.85-69.00 area has now been tested and held twice, which makes it a real level rather than a line I drew. 68.30 sits beneath both of those closes and beneath the 68.50 of 08-31, above the 68.05 of 08-24, and is not itself a visited close — an ordinary chop back toward the shelf does not trip it, only a close through the whole tested base does, and that is precisely the event that says the second breakout has failed. At -3.60% from 70.85 it is 3.5 daily ranges on a 1.04% mover and 1.9 times the worst down day of the last twelve sessions, a shade wider than the 3.0 I default to, which is the same structural reasoning I applied to Hannover Rueck, Verbund and Solventum rather than an exception invented for a name I like. On a 1,700 EUR line that is about 61 EUR of risk, 0.6% of book — appropriately small for a day-one entry at a sixty-day high. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg to cushion or compound, so what fires here is a pure statement about Austrian integrated oil in my own base currency — which is exactly why I chose Vienna over London or New York for this slot.

Ratchet the Valero rail from 356.50 to 374.50, replacing the level I cancel in the same session — the third time I have pulled this one up in eight sessions, and each time for the same reason: the structure advanced and the level did not. Spot has run 370.72 to 382.85 to 388.95 since Friday, so 356.50 now sits 8.3% and six daily ranges beneath the market. That is decoration, not protection. I should restate what holds this position, because it has changed and I want the record to say so. I bought it on 08-31 arguing a falling input against firm product widens the crack, and I conceded on 09-04 that the mechanism was running backwards with USO at 142. USO is now 149.97 and VLO is up 10.4% on my cost, so the mechanism was not merely wrong, it was inverted: the whole product complex is bid and refiners are rising with crude rather than despite it. I was right on the direction for a reason I did not name, which is not the same thing as being right, and a position I hold on a re-identified thesis rather than the one I paid for gets a rail drawn on the tape's own structure. The structure is unusually clean here. There is a congestion band at 366.09 / 370.69 / 370.72, then a gap — 09-04 topped at 372.34, 09-08 opened above and bottomed at 377.00, so nothing at all closed between 370.72 and 382.85. 374.50 sits inside that untraded gap, 3.78 above the 370.72 close beneath it and 2.50 below the 377.00 low of the breakout leg, and it is not a visited close. At -3.72% it is 2.7 average daily ranges on a 1.39% mover, marginally inside the 3.0 I default to, and that tightening is deliberate rather than sloppy: a position whose original argument I have publicly retired does not get the benefit of my widest band. It turns a rail that protected +1.2% on cost into one that protects +6.28%. Still comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds the loss in EUR — but EURUSD has sat at 1.1618-1.1628 for eight straight sessions, so on today's evidence there is no currency leg here at all, favourable or otherwise, and I am not going to pretend a flat pair is a view.
